meta_description: Exception handling on governed agents — 68% of exceptions auto-resolved and the customer-promise recovery loop runs itself

blocks.x: Exception handling on governed agents, 68% of exceptions auto-resolved and the customer-promise recovery loop runs itself

Identity withheld, a parcel operator whose exception queue was the network's confession: every scan that didn't match the plan, waiting for a human to decide what to tell whom. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline week measured the confession: 9,400 exceptions daily across hubs, median resolution 4.7 hours, and 23% of customer notifications sent after the customer had already called.

Exceptions resolved by whoever saw them first, against rules that lived in supervisors' heads. The same misroute at two hubs got two different answers, and neither one reached the customer's app in time.

We moved exceptions to governed agents: each exception classified against the play library with required actions, reroute, re-label, notify, escalate, executed in sequence, ambiguous cases routed to hub supervisors with the evidence attached, and the customer promise updated the moment the network knows. The play library is versioned; supervisors own its edits.
